title: Four hand-rolled hex encoders, two of which allocate a String per byte
description:
Lowercase-hex encoding is open-coded in four places, in two different styles:

Fold-with-write! style (correct, one allocation):
- persona-core/src/consumer.rs:50-54
- persona-core/src/pseudonym.rs:18-22

Allocate-per-byte style:
- persona-attestors/src/did_key.rs:39   `hash[..8].iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()`
- persona-attestors/src/fido2.rs:52     `hash[..8].iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()`

What goes wrong: the did_key/fido2 form heap-allocates and drops 8 short Strings per call before building the result — pure waste for a fixed 16-char output. More importantly, four copies of the same primitive means the two styles have already drifted, and a fifth caller will pick whichever it copies from.

Rewrite (no new dependency — `hex` is not in the workspace and does not need to be): add one small pub fn to persona-core, e.g.

    pub fn hex_lower(bytes: &[u8]) -> String

with the existing fold-with-write! body from pseudonym.rs, and have all four call sites use it. persona-attestors already depends on persona-core, so this deletes three implementations and adds none. This is net deletion, not a new abstraction layer.
close_reason: Duplicate of persona-5s4b.95 (same defect, filed by a second review agent from a different angle). Merged during review triage; reopen if the angle in this issue is not covered there.
